note: The relationship attack: speakers[0].name is swapped for a DIFFERENT, individually-real quote — this single-speaker transcript has no second person's name to steal, so the nearest equivalent is the tool name "Dexter" — while the original establishing `evidence` span ("my name is Sara", [7,22)) is left untouched. The new name quote is byte-real (span [63,69) really is "Dexter"), so SPAN_TEXT_MISMATCH does not fire; it is caught only because check 5.1 requires the name span to sit INSIDE its own evidence span, and [63,69) is nowhere near [7,22). Two individually-correct quotes that have nothing to do with each other do not make a speaker.
